title: Sim button box
summary: Two-part box for 6 push buttons, 2 toggle switches and 2 rotary encoders, with a USB port and slots to bolt it to the rig.
purpose: Gives riders and the operator real switches for things like engine start, lights and view reset, instead of a keyboard.

print.supports: None: print the body open side up and the lid top face down
print.orientation: Body: floor on the bed. Lid: flat face on the bed so the panel comes out smooth.

steps: Started from a rounded box and hollowed it with an even 3 mm wall, open at the top.
Added four corner posts with 4.0 mm holes sized for M3 heat-set inserts, so the lid can come off many times without wearing the plastic.
Cut a USB port in the back wall and two slots in the floor for M6 bolts to the rig.
Made the lid with a lip that drops 3 mm inside the walls (0.3 mm gap all round) so it locates itself.
Cut the panel holes: 12 mm buttons, 6.2 mm toggles, 7.2 mm encoders, then countersunk the M3 lid screw holes.
Chamfered the bottom edge 0.8 mm so the first layer squish (elephant foot) doesn't stop the lid fitting.
learning: Design clearances: parts that slide together need about 0.2 to 0.3 mm gap per side on an FDM printer. The lid lip uses 0.3 mm.
Heat-set inserts beat screwing into plastic. Hole sizes come from the insert maker; 4.0 mm suits common M3 x 5.7 mm inserts.
Print panels face-down on the bed: the side people see gets the smooth bed finish.
Make hole sizes a parameter. Switches vary, and changing one number is quicker than redrawing.
assumptions: Hole sizes assume 12 mm push buttons, MTS-style toggles (6 mm thread) and EC11 encoders (7 mm thread). Measure yours and change the numbers if different.
Mounting slots assume M6 bolts. The box's position on the rig hasn't been decided.

title: VR headset hook
summary: Bolts to 40 mm aluminium profile with two M8 T-nuts. A wide, rounded saddle holds the headset by its strap without creasing it.
purpose: Gives the headset a safe home between sessions, off the floor and away from the moving seat.

print.orientation: On its side (the 40 mm wide face down), so the arm's layers run the length of the hook and don't snap off.

steps: Drew the side view: a back plate, an arm reaching 75 mm out and a raised lip at the end.
Added a curved brace under the arm to spread the load into the back plate.
Pushed the profile out 40 mm wide to match the profile face.
Rounded every edge the strap touches (3 mm) so it can't dig in, and drilled two 8.5 mm holes 20 mm apart for M8 bolts.
learning: Fillets on the inside corner of a bracket make it far stronger: sharp inside corners are where cracks start.
Bolt holes: add about 0.5 mm to the bolt size (8.5 mm for M8) so the bolt slides through.
For brackets, print so the load runs along the layers, never trying to peel them apart.
assumptions: Assumes 40 mm aluminium profile and M8 T-nuts. Check what the rig frame uses before printing.

title: Extrusion cable clip
summary: Pushes into the 8 mm slot of 40-series aluminium profile and holds a cable bundle up to 10 mm across. No screws needed.
purpose: Keeps actuator, USB and power cables tidy and away from moving parts of the motion rig.

print.orientation: On its side (the flat 10 mm face on the bed), so the springy legs bend along the layers, not across them.

steps: Drew the clip as a flat side profile, then pushed it out 10 mm thick.
Made a split stem 7.6 mm wide (0.3 mm smaller than the slot each side) with a 1.8 mm gap so the legs can squeeze together.
Added small barbs that spring out behind the slot lip to hold it in.
Added a C-shaped cradle on top with a 6 mm opening; cables push in and stay put.
learning: Print orientation decides strength. Layers stick to each other less well than plastic along a layer, so parts that flex should bend along the layers.
Snap fits work best in PETG or nylon. PLA is stiff and tends to crack.
Small parts print better at 100% infill; there's no room for infill pattern anyway.
assumptions: Assumes 40-series profile with an 8 mm slot (common B-type). Measure the slot opening on the rig; if it's 10 mm, change the slot width.
